task: Reference Sync: distinguish typed references relocated into new/changed files from genuinely removed references while preserving stale-consumer blocking.

operationalIntelligence.problemStatement: PR #666 moved shipping/payment presentation authority from src/app/oldal/[slug]/page.tsx into a newly added shared component. Plan Before Code passed, but Edit-Time Reference Sync treated every typed display reference removed from the old file as globally removed even when the same typed reference was explicitly added in another changed file. Because the new file does not exist at the base SHA, base lookup also emits fatal git-show noise. The result is hundreds of false stale consumers and an inflated Implementation Sync required set.
observableOutcomes: A typed reference removed from one changed file and explicitly added with the same kind/value in another changed or newly added file is recorded as a relocation rather than a removal.
Relocated references do not create stale-consumer or required-change findings merely because unchanged files also contain the same lexical value.
A genuinely removed typed reference that survives only in unchanged machine consumers still blocks exactly as before.
Files added after the base SHA are handled as absent-before state without fatal git-show diagnostics.
unresolvedRisks: Global suppression based only on repository presence would hide genuine stale consumers and is forbidden.
Cross-kind lexical equality must not count as relocation; kind and value must both match.
A same-value addition in an unrelated changed file could be mistaken for authority relocation unless provenance is restricted to explicit diff-added typed references.

in: Existing Reference Sync diff candidate extraction and typed-reference reconciliation.
Added-file/base-absence handling used by Reference Sync.
Adversarial regression proving relocation PASS and genuine stale consumer BLOCK.
out: New reference registry, new gate, or generic stale-consumer exception.
Weakening component-key, export-symbol, route, CSS or implementation-expression stale detection.

assuranceCeiling.rationale: Reference Sync is an edit-time fail-closed authority. The proven false positive blocks valid refactors, while an over-broad fix could create false negatives. The highest practical correction is typed diff-side relocation evidence with negative controls proving unchanged stale consumers remain blockable.

acceptanceCriteria: Removed candidate kind/value pairs are suppressed from removedReferences only when the same kind/value is extracted from added diff lines in another current changed path.
Relocation provenance records from/to paths and remains transaction-local; repository-wide grep presence alone never proves relocation.
A same-value unchanged consumer without an explicit added-side authority continues to produce DEV-BLOCK-REFERENCE-SYNC.
Added files absent at base are treated as empty before-state without stderr fatal diagnostics.
PR #666 replay drops the relocation-derived stale/reference required-set explosion without exceptions.
invariants: Reference Sync remains fail-closed for genuine stale machine consumers.
Typed identity is kind + value; lexical equality across different kinds is not relocation.
Component/export/route/schema/token detection semantics are not weakened.
No Product Owner or storefront-specific special case is introduced.

failureModes: Moved authority is interpreted as removed and every lexical peer becomes stale.
A broad relocation heuristic suppresses a genuinely stale consumer.
A newly added path causes noisy base-object lookup failures.
Same lexical value with different semantic kind is falsely paired.
edgeCases: Same candidate appears in multiple added changed files.
Old value survives only in unchanged tests or machine consumers.
Same value appears as display-text and route/component key.

alternatives.summary: Pair removed typed candidates with explicit added-side typed candidates in the same transaction.
alternatives.reason: Preserves provenance and stale detection without repository-wide presence heuristics.

alternatives.summary: Treat a removed candidate as preserved whenever grep finds it anywhere after the change.
alternatives.reason: A stale consumer itself would falsely prove preservation.

alternatives.summary: Add Reference Sync exceptions for the shipping/payment files.
alternatives.reason: Would hide a foundational capability defect and would not generalize to future refactors.

specialistReviews.finding: Reference identity reconciliation belongs inside the existing Reference Sync runtime.
specialistReviews.resolution: Extend diffData relocation semantics; do not add a registry or gate.

specialistReviews.finding: Suppressing candidates because they exist anywhere after the change would convert stale consumers into false proof.
specialistReviews.resolution: Require explicit added-side typed diff evidence with matching kind/value.

specialistReviews.finding: Existing stale-consumer adversarial coverage must remain negative control.
specialistReviews.resolution: Add relocation regression beside existing semantic Reference Sync tests and retain stale BLOCK assertion.

specialistReviews.finding: Base reads for A-status files are expected absence, not exceptional diagnostics.
specialistReviews.resolution: Make base file reads existence-aware/fail-silent without changing current-file reads.
evidence: PR #666 fatal git show base:new-file evidence

challenge.scenario: Reference moves from an existing file to a newly added file.
challenge.finding: Current candidate filter checks only the old origin path and falsely calls the reference removed.
challenge.resolution: Pair typed removed/added diff candidates across changed paths.

challenge.scenario: Old value survives only in an unchanged test.
challenge.finding: Global presence cannot distinguish stale consumer from relocation authority.
challenge.resolution: Only added-side changed-file evidence can prove relocation.

challenge.scenario: Same text exists in an unrelated changed file as a different semantic kind.
New file is queried at the base SHA.
challenge.finding: git show reports expected absence as fatal noise.
challenge.resolution: Use diff status/base-path knowledge or silent base read so A status has empty before-state.

challenge.scenario: A component key is genuinely renamed and stale consumers retain the old key.
challenge.finding: The fix must not downgrade existing strong stale detection.
challenge.resolution: No matching old key on added side means candidate remains removed and consumers block.
Record all matching added current paths while suppressing only the removed-candidate classification.

proofPlan: Run plan-only Plan Before Code before implementation.
Regression-test typed display-text relocation into an A-status file and assert no stale block from unrelated unchanged peers.
Negative-control a genuine component-key/export-style removal with unchanged machine consumer and assert BLOCK remains.
Run exact-head Edit-Time, Quality, TypeScript, Production Build and Completion Truth; then CLOSE→LEARN before merge.
After merge replay PR #666 unchanged in product intent and require Reference Sync/Implementation Sync PASS.

requirements.requirement: Reference Sync recognizes transaction-local typed reference relocation into another changed/new file without converting unchanged lexical peers into stale consumers.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: A genuinely removed typed reference with an unchanged machine consumer must still BLOCK.

requirements.requirement: Reference Sync treats an A-status file as absent before the base SHA without fatal base-object lookup behavior.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: Expected absence of an added file at the base may not surface as a fatal Reference Sync condition.

requirements.requirement: The exact implementation head passes TypeScript and production build after Reference Sync relocation semantics are extended.

forbiddenRegressions.statement: The correction must not introduce type or production build regressions.

notes: Targeted Reference Sync capability correction proven by PR #666 exact-head replay. No storefront implementation or gate weakening in this transaction.
